messages.content: What projects has Aaron built?

Aaron's portfolio includes Session (a pure-Rust DAW with native PipeWire support), Heard (an AI-powered mastering plugin), Fanboy (a saxophone EQ plugin), AppNow (an LLM CRUD generator), MOVE (an open-source macOS window tiler), and this portfolio site itself.
Show me Aaron's personal projects.

A few highlights: Session (DAW in Rust), Heard (AI mastering DAW plugin), Fanboy (sax-player EQ plugin), AppNow (LLM-based CRUD generator), MOVE (macOS window tiler on GitHub), Klear (KDE transparent windows), Thinger (video word-isolator), and a George-Carlin-trained GPT-2.
What is Session?

Session is a digital audio workstation Aaron is building in pure Rust for Windows, macOS, and Linux — beta coming soon. On Linux it connects directly to PipeWire as a client, ending a decade of DAWs requiring JACK, QJACKctl, or jack-pipewire bridges. Closed source.
Tell me about Aaron's DAW.
Session — a digital audio workstation in pure Rust for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Its native PipeWire client on Linux is a first: no more JACK bridges. Beta coming soon.
Does Aaron have an audio product?
Several — Session (a pure-Rust cross-platform DAW), Heard (an AI auto-mastering plugin), and Fanboy (a saxophone EQ plugin). All are closed source, with betas and sites coming soon.
What is Heard?

Heard is an AI-powered DAW plugin (VST, CLAP, AU) that listens to each track, auto-detects the instrument and genre, and applies mastering/mixing tailored to that context. It works on individual tracks or on the master bus and figures out which. Closed source.
Aaron has an AI mastering plugin?
Yes — it's called Heard. It listens to a track, auto-detects the instrument and genre, and applies context-aware mastering. Ships as VST, CLAP, and AU.
What is Fanboy?

Fanboy is a DAW plugin (VST, CLAP, AU) for saxophone players that EQs their sound to resemble their favorite player. Presets include Joshua Redman, Joe Lovano, Michael Brecker, and Scott Hamilton, among others. It can match against any track to learn its EQ and transcribe full tunes (still experimental).
A plugin for saxophone players?
Yes — Fanboy. It EQs your sax sound to resemble players like Joshua Redman, Joe Lovano, Michael Brecker, or Scott Hamilton, and can learn EQ from any reference track.
Is Fanboy open source?
Closed source for now, possibly going open. The website is coming soon.
What is AppNow?

AppNow uses open-source or paid LLM APIs with a constraint layer that reliably generates working CRUD applications from user input. Permissions and scope expansions are landing rapidly. Repo coming soon.
Has Aaron built an LLM app generator?
Yes — AppNow. It pairs LLM APIs with a constraint layer to reliably generate working CRUD apps from plain-English input.
What is MOVE?
MOVE is a free, open-source desktop organizer and window tiler for macOS. It's freedom-respecting and focused on fast keyboard-driven layout. Source: github.com/aaronrohrbacher/MOVE
Does Aaron have any macOS tools?
Yes — MOVE, an open-source window tiler and desktop organizer for macOS focused on keyboard-driven layout. github.com/aaronrohrbacher/MOVE
What is Klear?
Klear is a KDE Plasma KWin script that enables transparent windows on older hardware using the JavaScript compositor API. Source: github.com/AaronRohrbacher/klear_kwin
Has Aaron written anything for Linux?

Yes — Klear, a KDE Plasma KWin script for transparent windows on older hardware. Aaron has also shipped Linux native apps at Forbes AAC (Qt on Rust) and built Session to be cross-platform including Linux.
What is Thinger?
Thinger is a Python script that isolates every use of a given word or phrase in a video and compiles them into a new clip. As the kids say, it's keen. github.com/AaronRohrbacher/thinger
Has Aaron trained a GPT model?
Yes — a PyTorch GPT-2 implementation trained on George Carlin transcriptions. It responds to prompts in his style. Fair warning: utterly vile. github.com/AaronRohrbacher/ai
Aaron trained a George Carlin bot?
Yes — a PyTorch GPT-2 trained on Carlin transcriptions. It responds in his style. Aaron notes it's utterly vile. github.com/AaronRohrbacher/ai
What is Nuel API?

Nuel API provisions LAMP stacks and cloud resources to client accounts, automates billing and signup, and delivers a fast PHP experience. It was the backbone of Aaron's company Nuel Cloud Computing. github.com/AaronRohrbacher/nuel-api
Tell me about Aaron's portfolio site.

This site! It's a fork of Payton Jewell's React design refactored into Next.js with SSR, SST, and AWS. It includes a fine-tuned Qwen LLM running entirely in-browser via Transformers.js (ONNX) for the chat, Amazon Connect integration for live chat/voice/video handoff, and a music streaming section with S3 presigned URLs and a WaveSurfer playlist player.
What runs the chat on Aaron's site?
A fine-tuned LLM running entirely in your browser — no servers for inference. Aaron custom-trained it on his own resume and Q&A data so it can answer about his background without calling an API.
How is the portfolio site built?

Next.js with SSR, deployed via SST on AWS. The chat agent runs an in-browser fine-tuned LLM, Amazon Connect handles live handoff to Aaron, and a music section streams from S3 via presigned URLs with a WaveSurfer player.
Is Aaron's portfolio open source?
Yes — github.com/AaronRohrbacher/aaronRohrbacherPortfolio. The live site is at aaronrohrbacher.com.
Does Aaron build music software?

Yes — Session (a pure-Rust cross-platform DAW), Heard (AI-powered DAW plugin for auto-mastering), and Fanboy (a saxophone EQ plugin). He also plays saxophone and clarinet and is learning instrument repair.
What does Aaron build in Rust?
Session — a digital audio workstation in pure Rust for Windows, macOS, and Linux with a native PipeWire client. Aaron also rebuilt Forbes AAC's Windows and Linux native apps using Qt on Rust.
What PyTorch projects has Aaron built?
A GPT-2 trained on George Carlin transcriptions (github.com/AaronRohrbacher/ai) is public. He's also done custom fine-tuning of open-source LLMs for other applications.
Does Aaron have anything on GitHub?

Yes — github.com/aaronrohrbacher. Public projects include MOVE (macOS window tiler), Klear (KDE transparent windows), Thinger (video word isolator), ai (Carlin GPT-2), Nuel API, and this portfolio site.
What's Aaron's most ambitious project?
Arguably Session — a full digital audio workstation in pure Rust with a native PipeWire client on Linux, which no other DAW has done. Beta coming soon.
What AI products has Aaron built?

Heard (AI auto-mastering DAW plugin), Fanboy (AI-powered EQ matching for saxophone), AppNow (LLM-based CRUD app generator), and this site's in-browser fine-tuned chat. Plus a PyTorch GPT-2 trained on George Carlin for fun.
Is Aaron working on agentic AI?
Yes — Aaron describes himself as a senior software and DevOps engineer building agentic AI. He's custom-training open-source LLMs and building with AWS AI services, Claude, and OpenAI APIs.
What's Aaron's current focus?
Building agentic AI — custom-training open-source LLMs and integrating them into real-world products. He's seeking senior DevOps or AI platform roles.
What roles is Aaron looking for?
Senior DevOps or AI platform roles. Aaron is actively seeking and available to start immediately.
Does Aaron do machine learning?

Yes — Aaron does applied ML work: custom-training open-source LLMs with PyTorch, building conversational AI with Amazon Lex/Polly/Transcribe/Q, and shipping AI products like the Heard mastering plugin and Fanboy sax EQ.
What DAW plugins does Aaron make?
Two: Heard (AI auto-mastering across any track or master bus) and Fanboy (saxophone EQ matching players like Redman, Lovano, Brecker, and Hamilton). Both ship as VST, CLAP, and AU.
Does Aaron use VST/CLAP/AU?
Yes — his DAW plugins Heard and Fanboy both ship in VST, CLAP, and AU formats.
Is Session available now?
Not yet — beta is coming soon. Session is a pure-Rust DAW for Windows, macOS, and Linux with a native PipeWire client on Linux.
When is Heard coming out?
A website and release are coming soon for Heard. It's closed source for now.
Can I buy Fanboy?
The website for Fanboy is coming soon. It's closed source for now, possibly going open.
What does Nuel API do?
Nuel API provisions LAMP stacks and cloud resources, automates billing and signup, and delivers a fast PHP experience. It was the backbone of Aaron's company Nuel Cloud Computing.
Has Aaron built anything with Qt?
Yes — the Windows and Linux native apps at Forbes AAC are built with Qt on Rust, replacing their deprecated Cordova stack.
What is the PipeWire thing in Session?
On Linux, Session connects directly to PipeWire as a client — no JACK, no QJACKctl, no jack-pipewire bridges. Aaron notes this ends a decade of DAWs requiring those workarounds.
Does Aaron use LLM APIs?
Yes — AppNow uses open-source and paid LLM APIs (with a constraint layer for reliable CRUD generation), and Aaron has shipped with Anthropic Claude and OpenAI ChatGPT APIs across other work.
What saxophone players does Aaron like?
Based on his Fanboy plugin presets: Joshua Redman, Joe Lovano, Michael Brecker, and Scott Hamilton, among others.
Who designed Aaron's site?

The base React design is a fork of Payton Jewell's work. Aaron refactored it into Next.js with SSR, SST, and AWS, and added the in-browser chat, Amazon Connect integration, and music streaming section.
Does Aaron contribute to open source?
Yes — several public repos: MOVE (macOS window tiler), Klear (KDE transparent windows), Thinger (video word isolator), ai (Carlin GPT-2), Nuel API, and this portfolio site.
